title: Refuse to check a half-written file
statement: Before checking a file, confirm it is whole, such as ending where it must and holding its anchors, and refuse otherwise, because a truncated copy can pass every assertion.
example: Cut to 98% of its length, a file passed all 78 of an audit's assertions; cut to 70%, it failed 29.
detail: A Grade 3 reading build's patch scripts truncate a file and then write it, so a check that reads during a write gets a prefix, and its rulebook notes that a prefix scans cleanly. Measured on one audit by cutting the file: at 70% it failed 29 assertions, at 98% it reported all 78 passing with no sign anything was wrong, and at 95% it lost five call sites and still passed its census. That audit and a copy-editing check now refuse to run unless the file ends in its closing html tag and carries its anchor functions, deliberately not a size band, which would need editing at every change, and the rule is to believe a refusal over a green run.
against: The incident that first prompted the rule was traced to a load-order race in the player rather than a partial read, and "a mid-write read and a load-order race present identically" while needing opposite fixes (grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md, line 545); the truncation hazard itself rests on the deliberate cutting test.

evidence.quote: ALL 78 PASS with no sign anything was wrong
so an overlapping read returns a *prefix* — and a prefix scans cleanly
now refuse (exit 2) unless the file ends in `</html>` and carries its anchor functions
